tldr: BrowserAgent is a browser-native web agent that learns directly from real-time Playwright interactions using human-inspired actions (click, scroll, type) with a two-stage SFT+RFT training pipeline and explicit memory mechanism, achieving ~20% improvement over Search-R1 on multi-hop QA despite using only 5.3K training samples.
contributions: A scalable Ray-parallelized orchestration layer enabling 50+ episodes/minute on a 32-core server, overcoming Playwright's low throughput limitation

A minimal yet expressive set of atomic browser operations (click, hover, press, scroll, type, tab management, URL navigation, stop) that simulate human browsing without additional summarization models
A two-stage training pipeline (SFT followed by Rejection Fine-Tuning with reasoning path selection) using only 5.3K trajectories
An explicit memory mechanism storing key conclusions across steps to enable long-horizon multi-hop reasoning up to 30 steps
methods: BrowserAgent operates directly on raw web pages via Playwright using an accessibility tree observation, interacting through four action categories: page operations (click, hover, press, scroll, type), tab management (new_tab, tab_focus, close_tab), URL navigation (goto, go_back, go_forward), and completion (stop). Training uses 5.3K trajectories sampled from NQ (4K) and HotpotQA (1.3K multi-hop), collected via automated GPT-4.1-assisted multi-turn interaction (up to 6 steps for basic, up to 30 for complex). Stage 1 performs SFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Stage 2 samples four answers per question, filters via EM for correct/incorrect pairs, selects the correct answer with the most reasoning steps, mixes with SFT data, and fine-tunes further.
results: BrowserAgent-7B achieves approximately 20% improvement over Search-R1-Instruct on multi-hop QA tasks (HotpotQA, 2Wiki, Bamboogle). RFT consistently improves over SFT, especially on multi-hop tasks. The 7B model outperforms the 3B model across all benchmarks. Evaluation used both exact match (EM) and LLM-based consensus judgment (GPT-4.1, Gemini Flash 2.5, Claude Sonnet 3.7) across six benchmarks: NQ, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, and Bamboogle. The system achieves 50+ episodes/minute on a single 32-core server with 64 concurrent Playwright browsers.
limitations: Training dataset is limited to 5.3K trajectories, significantly smaller than prior work
Evaluation is restricted to a locally deployed 2022 Wikipedia dump, not the full open web
Context window constraints still require the memory mechanism to cap reasoning at 30 steps
EM alone may underestimate performance since semantically correct answers differing in surface form are penalized
Experiments were conducted with 3B and 7B models only due to computational resource constraints
